title: Inverse Functions
domain: Attributes of Functions and Their Inverses
standard_text: 2A.2B graph and write the inverse of a function using notation such as f^(−1)(x); 2A.2C describe and analyze the relationship between a function and its inverse (quadratic and square root, logarithmic and exponential), including the restriction(s) on domain, which will restrict its range; 2A.2D use the composition of two functions, including the necessary restrictions on the domain, to determine if the functions are inverses of each other
meta_desc: Free Algebra II inverse function worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.2B to 2A.2D: write f⁻¹(x), inverses of quadratic, square root, exponential and log functions, composition and checking inverses. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To find f⁻¹, swap x and y and solve for y.
key_sub: The range of f is the domain of f⁻¹.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To find an inverse, swap x and y, then solve for y. Write it as f−1(x).
  • The graph of f−1 is the reflection of f over the line y = x.
  • The domain of f is the range of f−1, and the range of f is the domain of f−1.
  • x2 needs a restricted domain (such as x ≥ 0) to have an inverse function: √x.
  • f and g are inverses when f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x2 + 3, x ≥ 0

Swap: x = y2 + 3

y = √(x − 3)

Answer: f−1(x) = √(x − 3), x ≥ 3

Example

f(x) = 2x + 5

Swap: x = 2y + 5

2y = x − 5

Answer: f−1(x) = log2(x − 5)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Undoing in the wrong orderUndo the last step first.
Keeping the same signThe inverse of + 5 is − 5.
Forgetting the domainThe range of f is the domain of f−1.

sets.title: Find the inverse of a function

items.e: Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: subtract 3, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x − 3).

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x + 34.
items.e: Swap: x = y + 34. Multiply by 4: 4x = y + 3. Then subtract 3: f−1(x) = 4x − 3.
Swap x and y: x = −2y + 8. Solve for y: subtract 8, then divide by −2. f−1(x) = −x + 82. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
Swap x and y: x = 2y + 7. Solve for y: subtract 7, then divide by 2. f−1(x) = x − 72. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
Swap x and y: x = −2y − 7. Solve for y: subtract −7, then divide by −2. f−1(x) = −x − 72. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
Swap: x = √(y − 9). Square: x² = y − 9, so y = x² + 9. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 9, for x ≥ 0.
Swap: x = √(y − 2). Square: x² = y − 2, so y = x² + 2. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 2, for x ≥ 0.
Swap: x = √(y − 8). Square: x² = y − 8, so y = x² + 8. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 8, for x ≥ 0.
Swap x and y: x = 2y + 3. Solve for y: subtract 3, then divide by 2. f−1(x) = x − 32. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = 3x.
items.e: Swap: x = 3y, so xy = 3 and y = 3x. This function is its own inverse. f−1(x) = 3x.
Swap: x = √(y − 6). Square: x² = y − 6, so y = x² + 6. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 6, for x ≥ 0.

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = 5x.
items.e: Swap: x = 5y, so xy = 5 and y = 5x. This function is its own inverse. f−1(x) = 5x.
Swap: x = √(y − 7). Square: x² = y − 7, so y = x² + 7. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 7, for x ≥ 0.

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = 1x.
items.e: Swap: x = 1y, so xy = 1 and y = 1x. This function is its own inverse. f−1(x) = 1x.

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x − 22.
items.e: Swap: x = y − 22. Multiply by 2: 2x = y − 2. Then add 2: f−1(x) = 2x + 2.
Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: add 6, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x + 6).

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x − 54.
items.e: Swap: x = y − 54. Multiply by 4: 4x = y − 5. Then add 5: f−1(x) = 4x + 5.

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x + 64.
items.e: Swap: x = y + 64. Multiply by 4: 4x = y + 6. Then subtract 6: f−1(x) = 4x − 6.
Swap x and y: x = 4y − 5. Solve for y: subtract −5, then divide by 4. f−1(x) = x + 54. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: add 3, divide by 2, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x + 32).
